Hi Jared / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate you walking us through the payments use case and the latency targets. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the auth/key-management side so we can prepare the technical deep-dive: 

Recap:
- You run server-side inference for transaction screening and also expect some client-initiated calls from mobile apps.
- Primary concerns: key leakage on client devices, rotation/expiry, audit logs, and separation of duties for embeddings/reranker calls.

Questions / items we want to confirm before the deep-dive:
1) Preferred auth model: do you want server-to-server service accounts with short-lived JWTs (recommended) or long-lived API keys for backend services?
2) Do you need user-scoped keys for mobile clients (and if so, do you plan to proxy through your backend)?
3) Rotation policy: what frequency do you aim for today (90d, 30d, other)? Do you require automatic rotation via KMS?
4) Any constraints on key storage (HSM/KMS requirement) or audit log retention?

Next steps I propose:
- Neha from our SE team will share a short tech note and SDK snippets for both API key and JWT flows.
- Evelyn (security) will send over our standard security questionnaire and outline our rotation/audit capabilities.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive week of Aug 10 to map flows and decide on token lifespan and scoping.

Can you confirm preferred auth model and who on your side should join the deep-dive (security, infra, mobile)?

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks, great summary. A few quick answers from our side: 

- We prefer service accounts + JWTs for server-to-server flows. For mobile, our current approach is to proxy all calls through our backend, so we don't want long-lived client keys on devices.
- Rotation: security likes 90 days for long-lived secrets, but we are open to shorter-lived tokens for session-level access.
- We care about automatic rotation hooks (KMS) and having a clear audit trail for token issuance and revocation.

Can Neha share a sample JWT exchange flow? Also, what's Redwood's recommended split between API keys vs service accounts for embeddings/rerankers (same key, or separate scoped service accounts)?

I'll have Priya (infra) and Ravi (security) on the deep-dive call if that works.

Thanks,

Hi Jared / Priya — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive. TL;DR: recommend service accounts + short-lived JWTs for server-to-server; keep embeddings/reranker scoped to dedicated service accounts or API keys with restricted scopes.

Details / recommendations:
- Auth models we support:
  • API keys (long-lived): simple to get started, good for server-only usage, must be rotated regularly and stored in KMS/secret manager.
  • OAuth2 client_credentials / JWT (recommended for S2S): short-lived tokens issued by Redwood, exchangeable via a service-account private key.
  • Scoped tokens: create separate service accounts for different workloads (inference, embeddings, reranker, tool-calling) to limit blast radius.

- Rotation / key management:
  • We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS) for storing private keys and support key versioning.
  • Redwood supports automatic key rotation for server-side keys and emits rotation events to audit logs.
  • Recommended defaults: short-lived JWTs (1h) for session tokens; rotate service-account private keys at least every 90 days; rotate long-lived API keys every 30-90 days depending on risk profile.

- Example flows (high level):
  1) Service account private key stored in customer KMS -> your backend uses it to create a signed JWT -> exchange JWT at Redwood token endpoint -> receive short-lived access token for inference calls.
  2) For embeddings/reranker: issue a separate service account or API key restricted to embedding scope to avoid cross-use.

- SDK snippet (Node, simplified):
  const { RedwoodAuth } = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const auth = new RedwoodAuth({ tokenEndpoint: 'https://api.redwood.com/token' });
  // exchange signed JWT for access token
  const access = await auth.exchangeJwt({ signedJwt: signedJwtPem });
  await client.predict({ model: 'redwood-ggml', token: access.access_token });

Attachments: I attached a short "redwood-authn-overview.pdf" with diagrams and a sample curl/Node flow. Also linking our SDK auth guide: https://docs.redwood.com/sdk/authn-guide

Let us know if you'd like us to provision a test service account in the demo org for the deep-dive.

-Neha

Subject: Security questionnaire and key rotation items

Jared / Priya — following up from Marissa's thread. I'm attaching our security questionnaire for your security team to review and a short list of items we commonly coordinate on for key management.

Action items / asks from your security team:
- Please complete the attached fintechco-security-questions.xlsx and return to us.
- Confirm whether you require HSM-backed keys (Y/N) and provide KMS ARN if yes.
- Confirm expected rotation windows for service-account keys and long-lived API keys. Our baseline requirements:
  • Service-account private key rotation: 90 days (minimum).
  • Long-lived API keys: rotate every 30-90 days depending on environment.
  • Audit logs: we require ingestion of token issuance/rotation events into your SIEM for production-critical workloads.

Notes on private deployment: if you plan to use Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), we can enable mutual TLS (mTLS) and customer-managed KMS for full key custody.

If helpful, I can join the Aug 10 deep-dive to go over the questionnaire.
